mission: Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.

stage2a.operation: BHMT remethylation has separate enzyme and tissue ownership from MTR; betaine chemistry is not a direct neurotransmitter or clinical outcome.

existing_findings.proposition: BHMT transfers a methyl group from betaine to homocysteine, forming methionine and dimethylglycine, without folate or vitamin B12 in that reaction, and uses an active-site zinc ion to activate homocysteine.

existing_source_assessments.label: Evans et al. (2002)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Human BHMT structures show methionine formation from betaine and homocysteine, with zinc activating homocysteine; oxidation that expels zinc rearranges the active site.

assessment.study: X-ray structures of human BHMT in an oxidised zinc-free form and a reduced zinc-bound form with a homocysteine-like bisubstrate analog.
assessment.population: Purified crystallised human BHMT; no cells, animals or human participants.
assessment.result: The enzyme forms methionine from betaine and homocysteine. Zinc activates homocysteine. The zinc-binding sequences sit at the ends of barrel strands, and a Cys217–Cys299 disulfide expels zinc.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Structures at 2.15 Å (zinc-free) and 2.05 Å (zinc-bound). No physiological effect size applies.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct structural evidence for the human reaction and for catalytic zinc.
assessment.limitations: Static structures establish catalytic geometry, not in-vivo flux, dietary zinc responsiveness, or a clinical outcome.

existing_source_assessments.label: Breksa and Garrow (1999)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Replacing any of Cys217, Cys299 or Cys300 with alanine abolished human BHMT activity and reduced zinc binding. The reaction produces methionine and dimethylglycine from betaine and homocysteine.

assessment.study: Site-directed mutagenesis of recombinant human liver BHMT, with activity and zinc-binding measurements.
assessment.population: Recombinant human BHMT protein expressed in bacteria; no human participants.
assessment.result: Cys217, Cys299 and Cys300 were identified as zinc ligands. Mutation of any one to alanine caused complete loss of activity and a significant reduction in zinc binding. The catalysed transfer is from betaine to homocysteine, yielding dimethylglycine and methionine.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Complete loss of activity for each alanine substitution. No human effect size applies.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct evidence that catalytic activity of human BHMT depends on those zinc ligands, and a clear statement of the reaction products.
assessment.limitations: Bacterial expression and purified-protein assays do not show that dietary zinc limits BHMT in human tissues.

existing_source_assessments.label: Obeid (2013)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Methyl-group flow through BHMT does not depend on folate or vitamin B12, although the pathway is most active in liver and kidney and talks to the folate route.

assessment.study: Narrative review of methyl-donor deficiency with emphasis on the BHMT pathway.
assessment.population: Review of human and animal methyl-donor studies; not a new experiment.
assessment.result: BHMT transfers a methyl group from betaine to homocysteine. The review states that methyl flow through this pathway is not dependent on folate or vitamin B12, while several cross-talk mechanisms exist. BHMT is particularly active in liver and kidney.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No new effect size. The review cites other studies for homocysteine and metabolite changes.
assessment.evidence_summary: Explicit pathway-level statement that folate and vitamin B12 are not required for methyl flow through BHMT.
assessment.limitations: A review cannot replace a flux assay. Some quantitative deficiency claims are attributed to other papers and were not re-adjudicated here.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Irreversible oxidation of choline to betaine is an upstream supply route for the BHMT substrate and is not itself the BHMT reaction.

existing_source_assessments.label: Obeid (2013)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Betaine can be formed by irreversible oxidation of choline via choline dehydrogenase and betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase, and BHMT then uses that betaine to remethylate homocysteine.

assessment.study: Narrative review of methyl-donor metabolism centred on BHMT.
assessment.population: Review of human and animal evidence; not a new enzyme assay.
assessment.result: The review states the two-enzyme oxidation of choline to betaine and the subsequent BHMT reaction. It treats the oxidation as irreversible.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No new effect size for the oxidation steps.
assessment.evidence_summary: Pathway-level evidence that choline oxidation supplies betaine upstream of BHMT.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis, not a direct demonstration of human choline dehydrogenase kinetics or of dietary choline increasing BHMT flux.

existing_source_assessments.label: Salvi and Gadda (2013)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Human choline dehydrogenase oxidises choline to betaine aldehyde, and betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase completes formation of betaine, which can donate a methyl group to homocysteine.

assessment.study: Review of human choline dehydrogenase localisation, physiological role and biochemical characterisation.
assessment.population: Review of human tissue activity and comparative biochemistry; not a dietary trial.
assessment.result: The enzyme sits in the inner mitochondrial membrane and is found mainly in kidney and liver. It oxidises choline to betaine aldehyde. A second enzyme, betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase, oxidises that aldehyde to betaine. Betaine is described as a methyl donor for methionine formation from homocysteine. Purified active human enzyme has been difficult to obtain.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Tissue activity was reported mainly in kidney, with about six-fold lower activity in liver. No dietary dose-response was measured.
assessment.evidence_summary: Enzyme-level support for the two-step oxidation that supplies betaine.
assessment.limitations: Incomplete purification of human choline dehydrogenase limits kinetic detail. Localisation and pathway role do not show that dietary choline changes BHMT flux.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Changes in plasma homocysteine after betaine supplementation, choline depletion, or vitamin B12 and fish-oil treatment do not measure tissue BHMT flux and do not establish a clinical benefit of this reaction.

existing_source_assessments.label: Olthof et al. (2003)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Daily betaine at 1.5, 3 and 6 g lowered fasting plasma homocysteine by about 12%, 15% and 20% versus placebo after six weeks, without a measurement of tissue BHMT flux.

assessment.study: Randomised, placebo-controlled trial of anhydrous betaine for six weeks, with methionine-load tests.
assessment.population: Four groups of 19 healthy adults selected for higher plasma homocysteine within a broad reference range.
assessment.result: Fasting plasma homocysteine after 1.5, 3 and 6 g/day was about 12%, 15% and 20% lower than placebo. The post-load rise was also smaller. The discussion infers increased betaine-dependent remethylation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About 12% (P < 0.01), 15% (P < 0.002) and 20% (P < 0.0001) lower fasting homocysteine than placebo at six weeks for 1.5, 3 and 6 g/day.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human evidence that supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine. The endpoint is a circulating metabolite, not enzyme flux.
assessment.limitations: No BHMT activity, tissue methionine flux, dimethylglycine production rate, or clinical symptom outcome was measured.

existing_source_assessments.label: da Costa et al. (2005)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Choline deficiency raised post-methionine-load plasma homocysteine in mice and in a small human pilot, but did not measure BHMT activity, and mouse liver betaine did not fall.

assessment.study: Three-week mouse diets with 0, 10 or 35 mmol choline/kg, plus a depletion-repletion pilot in men, each with an oral methionine load.
assessment.population: Male C57BL/6J mice and eight healthy men aged 20–46 years.
assessment.result: Two hours after the load, choline-deficient mice had about twice the plasma homocysteine of choline-fed mice. Fasting values did not differ. Four hours after the load, clinically choline-depleted men had plasma homocysteine about 35% higher than when not depleted. Hepatic betaine in the mice was not significantly lower.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About twofold higher post-load homocysteine in deficient mice. About 35% higher post-load homocysteine in depleted men. Mouse liver betaine 1.3 ± 0.3 versus 1.1 ± 0.3 nmol/mg protein.
assessment.evidence_summary: Dietary choline depletion can change post-load plasma homocysteine. It does not isolate BHMT flux, and the mouse betaine pool was not shown to fall.
assessment.limitations: Human sample of eight men, clinical depletion rather than ordinary intake, and no enzyme or tracer measurement.

existing_source_assessments.label: Huang et al. (2015)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Vitamin B12, fish oil and their combination lowered plasma homocysteine without any betaine intervention, so the biomarker is not specific to BHMT.

assessment.study: Randomised trial of vitamin B12, fish oil, or both, with plasma homocysteine as an endpoint.
assessment.population: Thirty-eight participants randomised to three groups.
assessment.result: The repository abstract reports plasma homocysteine reductions of about 22% with vitamin B12, 19% with fish oil, and 39% with the combination. Betaine and BHMT were not the interventions.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About 22%, 19% and 39% lower plasma homocysteine in the three arms.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows that plasma homocysteine can fall through inputs that are not the BHMT substrate.
assessment.limitations: The attached abstract does not report BHMT activity, betaine status or a clinical neurological outcome. Design detail beyond the abstract was not re-extracted.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: The repository ADHD diet review and choline neurodevelopment review do not directly demonstrate that BHMT-dependent remethylation changes Focus / Attention Stability.

existing_source_assessments.label: Millichap and Yee (2012)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Reviews dietary approaches to ADHD symptoms, including fatty acids, iron and zinc, and does not test BHMT or betaine supplementation.

assessment.study: Narrative clinical review of diet as a treatment factor in ADHD.
assessment.population: Children with ADHD in the reviewed literature; not a BHMT cohort.
assessment.result: Discusses restriction diets, fatty-acid supplements, iron, zinc and dietary pattern. No betaine dose, BHMT assay or homocysteine remethylation endpoint is the basis of the conclusions.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No BHMT or betaine effect size is reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows why an ADHD diet review cannot be used as direct evidence for this reaction.
assessment.limitations: Narrative review spanning many exposures and outcomes. Not a mechanism test.

existing_source_assessments.label: Derbyshire and Maes (2023)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Reviews choline in autism, ADHD and dyslexia, without measuring BHMT activity or betaine-dependent remethylation.

assessment.study: Narrative review of choline and neurodevelopmental disorders.
assessment.population: Pregnancy, children with autism, and people with ADHD or dyslexia in the reviewed literature.
assessment.result: Low choline intake or altered choline status is discussed for those groups. The review does not test BHMT, betaine supplementation or tissue remethylation flux against attention scores.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No BHMT effect size is reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: Choline neurodevelopment context is not a BHMT outcome study.
assessment.limitations: Narrative review. Choline has membrane and neurotransmitter roles outside this reaction.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Plasma homocysteine lowering after betaine, and narrative choline reviews, do not directly demonstrate that BHMT-dependent remethylation changes Cognitive Clarity.

existing_source_assessments.label: Olthof et al. (2003)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults and does not measure cognitive clarity or BHMT flux.

assessment.study: Six-week randomised betaine supplementation trial with methionine loads.
assessment.population: Healthy adults in four groups of 19.
assessment.result: Fasting and post-load plasma homocysteine fell relative to placebo. No cognitive clarity scale was used.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Fasting homocysteine about 12%, 15% and 20% lower than placebo at 1.5, 3 and 6 g/day. No cognitive effect size exists in the study.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human homocysteine evidence without a clarity endpoint.
assessment.limitations: Healthy adults, circulating endpoint, no cognitive measurement.

existing_source_assessments.label: Derbyshire and Maes (2023)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Discusses choline and neurodevelopment, not BHMT-dependent cognitive clarity.

assessment.study: Narrative review of choline in autism, ADHD and dyslexia.
assessment.population: Developmental cohorts in the reviewed literature.
assessment.result: Considers choline status and neurodevelopmental conditions. It does not isolate BHMT or measure cognitive clarity as a remethylation outcome.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No BHMT or clarity effect size for this reaction is reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: Neurodevelopment review, not a test of this PM against cognitive clarity.
assessment.limitations: Narrative review with several choline roles outside BHMT.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Inadequate betaine availability, including from conditional failure of choline provision, can constrain BHMT-dependent homocysteine remethylation capacity.

existing_source_assessments.label: da Costa et al. (2005)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Controlled choline depletion lowered plasma betaine and reduced post-methionine-load homocysteine-handling reserve in the participants who developed clinical depletion; both the phenotype and challenge response reversed with repletion.

assessment.study: Controlled depletion–repletion pilot with a methionine-load challenge.
assessment.population: Eight healthy men aged 20–46 years; four developed hepatic steatosis during depletion.
assessment.result: Plasma choline and betaine fell about 30% and 47% in the full group. In the four clinically depleted men, post-load homocysteine increased by 5.2 µmol/L (95% CI 1.2–9.1; P = 0.025) relative to the 550 mg/day baseline phase and returned to the baseline response after repletion. Folate did not fall.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Betaine fell from 66 ± 7 to 35 ± 2 nmol/mL in all eight men; clinically depleted participants had a 5.2 µmol/L greater post-load homocysteine response.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human intervention evidence linking choline inadequacy, lower betaine availability and reduced remethylation reserve under challenge.
assessment.limitations: Small male-only pilot, severe controlled depletion, shared circulating endpoint, and no direct tissue or isotope-resolved BHMT flux.

existing_source_assessments.label: Evans et al. (2002)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Human BHMT structures establish the betaine-to-homocysteine methyl transfer that links betaine availability to the challenged remethylation response.

assessment.study: X-ray structural analysis of human BHMT.
assessment.result: BHMT transfers a methyl group from betaine to homocysteine to form methionine and dimethylglycine.
assessment.evidence_summary: Provides reaction-specific attribution for the donor-pool intervention chain.
assessment.limitations: Purified-enzyme evidence does not itself establish dietary constraint.

existing_source_assessments.label: Setoue et al. (2008)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Under low-methionine conditions, choline deprivation depleted hepatic betaine and raised plasma homocysteine; either choline or betaine suppressed the phenotype.

assessment.study: Controlled rat feeding experiments varying choline, methionine context and lipotrope rescue.
assessment.population: Male Wistar rats fed casein- or soybean-protein-based diets.
assessment.result: On the choline-deprived soybean-protein diet, hepatic betaine fell from about 3.65 to 0.13 µmol/g and plasma homocysteine rose from about 12.5 to 33.5 µmol/L. Choline or betaine supplementation restored hepatic betaine to about 9.81 or 13.3 µmol/g and lowered plasma homocysteine to about 7.3 or 7.7 µmol/L. Ex-vivo BHMT activity did not decline.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Approximately 96% lower hepatic betaine with deprivation; rescue restored the pool above control and suppressed hyperhomocysteinaemia.
assessment.evidence_summary: Pool depletion and rescue connect conditional choline inadequacy to loss of substrate-supported remethylation capacity rather than loss of BHMT protein competence.
assessment.limitations: Rat liver model under low-methionine conditions; homocysteine removal also involved transsulfuration, and no in-vivo isotope-resolved BHMT flux was measured.

existing_source_assessments.label: Strakova et al. (2011)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Specific pharmacological BHMT inhibition produced the pathway direction expected when BHMT-dependent capacity fails.

assessment.study: Rat feeding study using the potent and specific BHMT inhibitor S-(δ-carboxybutyl)-L-homocysteine for 3 or 14 days across adequate, cysteine-free and methionine-deficient diets.
assessment.result: The inhibitor reduced liver BHMT activity by more than 90%, increased plasma homocysteine two- to five-fold and lowered hepatic SAM by more than 40% across dietary conditions.
assessment.effect_magnitude: >90% lower BHMT activity; 2–5-fold higher plasma homocysteine; >40% lower liver SAM.
assessment.evidence_summary: Specific perturbation confirms that impaired BHMT capacity can generate the observed remethylation and methylation-state direction.
assessment.limitations: Pharmacological inhibition in rats does not quantify the effect of ordinary human betaine or choline intake.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

preserved_phenome_source_records.rationale: Reviews of ADHD diets and of choline in neurodevelopment discuss attention, but they do not test BHMT activity or betaine supplementation as an attention treatment {{cite:millichap_diet_2012,derbyshire_role_2023}}. The enzyme reaction is established separately, and a change in plasma homocysteine is not an attention outcome {{cite:evans_betaine_2002,olthof_low_2003}}. Direct evidence that this remethylation route changes Focus / Attention Stability remains a gap.

Lower plasma homocysteine after betaine supplements is a blood measurement, not a test of cognitive clarity or of tissue BHMT activity {{cite:olthof_low_2003}}. A choline review discusses neurodevelopment rather than an effect of this reaction on clarity {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. The relationship remains an indirect bridge with no direct outcome evidence.
